title: Rav Shmuel bar Marta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Bava Batra 52a records a dispute over whether Marta is a man’s or a woman’s name. Rashbam explains that Marta was Rabbi Chiyya’s brother, as in Sanhedrin 5a; Rabbeinu Gershom takes it as a woman’s name, Rabbi Chiyya’s sister.
And Rav Shmuel received [teachings] from Rav, as in Pesachim 113b:
Rabbah bar bar Chana reports Rav Shmuel bar Marta reporting Rav.
And in Jerusalem Talmud Challah ch. 1, halakhah 3: Rabbi Yitzchak in the name of Rav Shmuel bar Marta in the name of Rav: "Challah, they have separated" etc.
And Megillah 15b: Rav said, and some say Rav Shmuel bar Marta [said].
Bava Kamma 51b likewise has Rabbah bar bar Chana reporting Rav Shmuel bar Marta.
And we find Rabbi Ila, son of Rav Shmuel bar Marta, in Berakhot 13b.
Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta, Berakhot 25b.

notes.text: Whether Marta is the father’s or mother’s name remains the commentators’ dispute. The heading’s title Rav is followed; the checked Pesachim passage prints Rabbi Shmuel.

The consulted Vilna Rashbam on Bava Batra 52a explains Marta as a male sage, Rabbi Chiyya’s brother. The consulted Rabbeinu Gershom says “of so-and-so’s wife,” supporting a woman’s name; that short gloss does not itself specify Chiyya’s sister. The latter relationship remains Hyman’s report. Pesachim 113b uses Rabbi Shmuel, while Hyman’s heading supplies Rav; no global title harmonization is made.
